subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Registers: Groups of Flip-Flops
description: A quick win: understand Registers: Groups of Flip-Flops.

hook.text: Line up 64 flip-flops and you get a 64-bit register — one word of CPU storage.

buildup.text: All flip-flops share the same clock. On each edge, the entire word updates at once.

discovery.text: CPUs have dozens of registers: program counter, instruction register, general-purpose registers.

twist.text: Registers are the fastest memory — accessed in a single clock cycle, unlike cache or RAM.

climax.text: ARM's architecture has 31 general-purpose 64-bit registers — the core of its data path.

punchline.text: Flip-flops in a row — the fastest memory a processor has.

quiz.question: Why are registers faster than cache or RAM?
options: They use larger transistors that switch more quickly
They are built from flip-flops directly inside the CPU, accessed in one clock cycle
They store data in analog form, avoiding digital conversion delays
